papers.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
papers.tldr: Get most of TRPO's stability with a first-order method: clip the probability ratio $r_t(\theta)$ so one update cannot move the policy too far.
papers.summary:
Policy-gradient methods are unstable when we take several gradient steps on the same batch: the policy can drift far from the one that collected the data. \textbf{TRPO} fixes this with a KL trust-region constraint, but needs second-order machinery (conjugate gradient, line search).

PPO replaces the constraint by a \emph{clipped surrogate objective}. With the probability ratio $r_t(\theta) = \pi_\theta(a_t\mid s_t)/\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(a_t\mid s_t)$ and an advantage estimate $\hat A_t$,
\[
  L^{\text{CLIP}}(\theta) = \hat{\E}_t\!\left[\min\!\big(r_t(\theta)\hat A_t,\ \operatorname{clip}(r_t(\theta), 1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon)\,\hat A_t\big)\right].
\]
Taking the minimum makes the objective a \emph{pessimistic} bound on the unclipped one, so there is no incentive to push $r_t$ outside $[1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon]$. This allows $K$ epochs of minibatch SGD per batch of data. On MuJoCo and Atari it matches or beats TRPO and A2C while being a few lines of code.

papers.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
papers.tldr: The KL-regularised RLHF optimum is available in closed form, so preference learning becomes a logistic loss on $\log\frac{\pi_\theta}{\pi_{\text{ref}}}$ differences --- no reward model, no RL.
papers.summary:
RLHF fits a reward model to preference data and then optimises a KL-regularised objective with RL (PPO) --- complex, unstable and expensive. DPO observes that the optimal policy of the KL-regularised problem has a closed form, so the reward can be \emph{re-parameterised through the policy}. Plugging this into the Bradley--Terry likelihood gives a simple classification loss on preference pairs: no reward model, no sampling during training, no RL.
\[
\mathcal{L}_{\text{DPO}}(\pi_\theta; \pi_{\text{ref}}) = -\E_{(x, y_w, y_l)\sim\mathcal{D}}\left[\log \sigma\!\left(\beta \log\frac{\pi_\theta(y_w\mid x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y_w\mid x)} - \beta \log\frac{\pi_\theta(y_l\mid x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y_l\mid x)}\right)\right]
\]
It matches or beats PPO-based RLHF on controlled sentiment generation, summarisation (Reddit TL;DR) and single-turn dialogue (Anthropic HH), while being far more stable and cheaper to tune.

papers.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
papers.tldr: SFT $\to$ reward model $\to$ PPO on GPT-3: labelers prefer the 1.3B InstructGPT over the 175B GPT-3.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.tldr: Learn to reverse a fixed Gaussian noising chain by predicting the noise: $\|\epsilon - \epsilon_\theta(x_t, t)\|^2$ is all you train on.
papers.summary: A diffusion model is a latent-variable model trained to invert a fixed Markov chain that gradually adds Gaussian noise to data. With a particular parameterisation --- predicting the \emph{noise} $\epsilon$ rather than the posterior mean --- the variational bound reduces to a simple denoising objective, which connects diffusion models to denoising score matching and annealed Langevin dynamics. The resulting samples are of very high quality (FID $3.17$ on unconditional CIFAR-10).

papers.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
papers.tldr: Diffusion and score matching as SDEs: sample by solving the reverse-time SDE, or a probability-flow ODE that gives exact likelihoods.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.tldr: Replace recurrence with multi-head self-attention: fully parallel training and better translation quality.
papers.summary: The Transformer drops recurrence and convolutions and models sequences with \emph{attention only}. Each layer combines multi-head self-attention with a position-wise feed-forward network, residual connections and layer normalisation; word order enters through sinusoidal positional encodings. Because all positions are processed in parallel, training is much faster than for recurrent seq2seq models, and it set a new state of the art on WMT'14 English--German (28.4 BLEU) and English--French translation.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
papers.tldr: Language-model loss follows smooth power laws in parameters, data and compute across many orders of magnitude.
